headline: New law requires HHS to create and carry out a national plan to prevent, treat, and cure Parkinson's disease, running through 2035.
what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to run a project on Parkinson's disease and related conditions, including a national plan that it must carry out and update over time. The plan is meant to coordinate federal work on preventing, diagnosing, treating, and curing the disease, and on improving care. HHS must also review each year how well the country is preparing for the growing number of people with Parkinson's. The law creates an advisory council of federal and non-federal members to give HHS recommendations.

who_it_affects.group: People with Parkinson's disease and related conditions
who_it_affects.how: Federal efforts to improve their diagnosis, treatment, and care will be organized under a single national plan.

who_it_affects.group: Families and caregivers of people with Parkinson's
who_it_affects.how: They may be affected by HHS efforts to improve care for people with the disease.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Health and Human Services
who_it_affects.how: HHS must create and update a national plan, assess preparedness every year, and work with a new advisory council.

who_it_affects.group: Parkinson's researchers, doctors, and advocacy groups
who_it_affects.how: Non-federal experts and stakeholders can serve on the new council that advises HHS.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 2, 2024; its provisions end at the close of 2035.
